title: Completing the Square and Vertex Form
seo_title: Algebra II Completing the Square and Vertex Form Worksheets (TEKS 2A.4D)
domain: Quadratic and Square Root Functions, Equations, and Inequalities
standard_text: 2A.4D transform a quadratic function f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c to the form f(x) = a(x − h)^2 + k to identify the different attributes of f(x)
meta_desc: Free Algebra II worksheets for Texas TEKS 2A.4D: complete the square, write quadratics in vertex form, find the vertex, axis, maximum or minimum and range. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: f(x) = a(x − h)² + k has vertex (h, k).
key_sub: Complete the square: add and subtract (b ÷ 2)².
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Vertex form: f(x) = a(x − h)2 + k. The vertex is (h, k) and the axis of symmetry is x = h.
  • To complete the square for x2 + bx, add and subtract (b ÷ 2)2.
  • If a ≠ 1, factor a out of the x-terms first. The square you add inside is worth a times as much outside.
  • a > 0: minimum value k. a < 0: maximum value k.

Examples

Example

f(x) = x2 − 6x + 11

(−6 ÷ 2)2 = 9

x2 − 6x + 9 − 9 + 11

Answer: (x − 3)2 + 2, vertex (3, 2)

Example

f(x) = 2x2 + 8x + 3

2(x2 + 4x + 4) + 3 − 8

Answer: 2(x + 2)2 − 5

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The wrong sign of h(x − 3)2 has h = 3; (x + 3)2 has h = −3.
Forgetting to multiply by aAdding 4 inside 2( ) adds 8.
Adding the square without subtracting itAdd and subtract the same amount.

faq.a: Transform a quadratic function f(x) = ax² + bx + c to the form f(x) = a(x − h)² + k to identify the different attributes of f(x).
It shows the vertex, axis of symmetry and maximum or minimum right away.

faq.q: Is there a shortcut for the vertex?
faq.a: Yes: x = −b ÷ (2a), then find f of that value.

faq.q: Does a change when you complete the square?
faq.a: No. a is the same in both forms.
